page: UpCloud PREMIUM-4xCPU-8GB is a Premium family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 4 vCPUs and 4 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz under a shared CPU allocation model. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, alongside 100 GB of local SSD storage. Network connectivity is supported by one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scores all placing in the top tier. Multi-core performance, including Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core, falls within the average range. However, memory performance presents a distinct tradeoff; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 818.19 GB/sec, the PassMark memory score is weak, placing in the bottom quarter of tested systems.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server offers a cost-effective entry point for compute-focused workloads that do not require dedicated CPU pinning. It is well-suited for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight web serving, and software compilation. It is less optimal for memory-intensive databases or larger large language model inference, as demonstrated by weak prompt processing speeds on 7B models.
